html:
A rabbi and mystic from Smyrna, now İzmir, who was proclaimed the Messiah in 1665 and set off the largest messianic movement in Jewish history.

Zevi studied Kabbalah and had long made strange claims. In 1665 a young prophet, Nathan of Gaza, declared him the Messiah. The news spread through letters and printed pamphlets across the Ottoman Empire and to Jewish communities in Italy, Amsterdam, Poland and beyond. Many sold their goods to prepare for the return to the Holy Land. His followers became known as Sabbateans.

In 1666 he sailed for Istanbul, was arrested, and was brought before the court of Sultan Mehmed IV at Edirne. Given the choice of death or Islam, he converted. Most followers were crushed; some decided his conversion was part of a hidden plan. He died in exile in Ulcinj, in today's Montenegro, in 1676.

A group in Salonica followed him into Islam and kept secret rites for generations, the Dönmeh. The shock of his fall made rabbis wary of messianic claims for a long time.
sum: A rabbi and mystic from Smyrna, now İzmir, who was proclaimed the Messiah in 1665 and set off the largest messianic movement in Jewish history.
